results.title: Album Reviews · Cureation
results.bodyText:
HOME
REVIEWS
Reviews

Fourteen studio albums. Fourteen close listens. Long-form criticism written for fans who know the songs and still want to hear them differently.

9.5
/ 10
FEATURED REVIEW · 2024
Songs of a Lost World: An ending that opens outward

After sixteen years, The Cure returned with an album of grief and mortality that feels monumental because it never mistakes scale for spectacle.

BY BERNARD MCWEENEY
2 MIN READ
READ THE FULL REVIEW
→
COMPLETE STUDIO ARCHIVE
Every album reviewed
14 REVIEWS
7.3
2008 · 2 MIN
4:13 Dream: Colour after the storm

Bright guitars and direct melodies give The Cure’s thirteenth album an appealing lift, even when the larger design feels unfinished.

READ REVIEW →
6.9
2004 · 2 MIN
The Cure: Raw edges, mixed results

The self-titled album pushes The Cure toward a harsher, more immediate sound, gaining force while sacrificing some of their mystery.

READ REVIEW →
8.5
2000 · 2 MIN
Bloodflowers: The beauty of the long goodbye

Patient and autumnal, Bloodflowers finds The Cure returning to long-form melancholy without pretending the past can be repeated.

READ REVIEW →
7.1
1996 · 2 MIN
Wild Mood Swings: The argument for inconsistency

The Cure’s most disputed album is overstuffed and tonally unstable, but its risks deserve more than a dismissive verdict.

READ REVIEW →
9.2
1992 · 2 MIN
Wish: Bright light, deep water

At their commercial peak, The Cure made a record that holds euphoria and collapse in the same wide-open sound.

READ REVIEW →
10
1989 · 2 MIN
Disintegration: The masterpiece that keeps moving

Immense yet intimate, Disintegration turns time, memory and romantic fear into The Cure’s most complete album.

READ REVIEW →
9
1987 · 2 MIN
Kiss Me, Kiss Me, Kiss Me: Desire in every direction

The Cure’s great double album is excessive, romantic, abrasive and alive—the catalogue at its most gloriously plural.

READ REVIEW →
9
1985 · 2 MIN
The Head on the Door: Ten songs, a whole world

Compact, varied and endlessly replayable, The Head on the Door turns The Cure’s contradictions into pop perfection.

READ REVIEW →
7.5
1984 · 2 MIN
The Top: Fever dreams and loose ends

Messy by design and fascinating in practice, The Top catches Robert Smith rebuilding The Cure in public.

READ REVIEW →
9.3
1982 · 2 MIN
Pornography: No exit, no wasted motion

The Cure’s darkest record remains overwhelming because its chaos is shaped with absolute purpose.

READ REVIEW →
8.7
1981 · 2 MIN
Faith: The long grey afternoon

Slow, severe and quietly beautiful, Faith turns doubt and grief into an album of remarkable physical presence.

READ REVIEW →
8.8
1980 · 2 MIN
Seventeen Seconds: Empty space, perfect tension

With one decisive turn toward silence, repetition and atmosphere, The Cure found a language that still feels entirely their own.

READ REVIEW →
7.4
1979 · 2 MIN
Three Imaginary Boys: The sound of a band becoming itself

Restless, sharp and not entirely under its creators’ control, The Cure’s debut is most compelling when the future briefly comes into focus.

READ REVIEW →

results.title: The wiki · Cureation
results.bodyText:
HOME
THE WIKI
The wiki

Long-form reference articles, deeper than a liner note and shorter than a biography, cross-referenced to everything else in the archive.

ARTICLES
5
SORT
A–Z
5 ARTICLES
A living reference,
not a filing cabinet.

Stories, people, places and ideas are connected back to the records, songs and shows they belong to.

01
REFERENCE ARTICLE
From Easy Cure to The Cure, 1978

How a Crawley four-piece dropped half their name — and most of their original set — in the year between signing with Hansa and releasing their first single on Fiction.

5 MIN READ
↗
02
REFERENCE ARTICLE
Robert Smith's guitars: a short ledger

The instruments that made the records — from the hand-me-down Top Twenty of 1977 to the Gibsons and Fenders that defined the imperial-era tone.

6 MIN READ
↗
03
REFERENCE ARTICLE
The Cure at Glastonbury: four headline slots

A short chronicle of the band's four Pyramid Stage headline appearances — 1986, 1990, 1995 and 2019 — and what each marked within the band's arc.

5 MIN READ
↗
04
REFERENCE ARTICLE
The Disintegration sessions, winter 1988–89

Recorded between November 1988 and February 1989 at Outside Studios in Berkshire and Hook End Manor in Oxfordshire, Disintegration took shape against the band's own stated intention to make something "darker and slower."

7 MIN READ
↗
05
REFERENCE ARTICLE
Why Pornography still sounds the way it does

A note on the production choices — drum treatment, flanging, mix-bus compression — that made The Cure's fourth album harder for the band to make and harder for their audience to place.

6 MIN READ
↗
